skills.name: Formal and informal letters: purpose and register

note.text: Letters adapt content, layout and register to recipient and purpose. A formal request to an unnamed official can pair Dear Sir or Madam with Yours faithfully in the British convention modelled here. A letter to a friend can use a personal greeting and friendly closing. Both require clear paragraphs and accurate information. Formality does not require inflated vocabulary; friendliness does not remove sentence boundaries. The teacher should confirm local address, date, length and closing requirements.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to write to a specified recipient with suitable register, a clear request and relevant support. Builds on: audience, purpose and prior letter layouts. Leads to: essay structure and directed writing.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Lower Sixth extension: compare a formal request to a school coordinator with a personal letter explaining the same club proposal to a friend. Preserve the facts while changing salutation, explanation and tone for each recipient. State what response is sought. A formal style is not an excuse for inflated or insulting language. The model pair and paper task below extend the Form Five letter foundation; teachers should confirm the required examination layout.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the audience, purpose and required content. Plan the order, draft in your own words and check each feature against the model. Explain why an edit improves the answer.

paper_task.prompt: Write a formal request to an unnamed school official for the notice-checking discussion, then an informal letter telling a friend about it. Preserve unconfirmed arrangements in both. Follow the teacher’s required layout and length.
model: Formal model: Reading Club, Fictional School, Bamenda. Date: the day of drafting. Dear Sir or Madam, I write for our club to request permission for a supervised discussion on checking school notices. We would like pupils to practise distinguishing confirmed details from suggestions.

The session would use original classroom examples and partner work. A teacher would need to confirm the venue and timing before invitations are issued. Please let us know whether the proposal can be considered and whom we should consult. Yours faithfully, Bih, Club secretary.

Informal model: Fictional School, Bamenda. Date: the day of drafting. Dear Amina, Our reading club is planning a discussion about checking notices. I thought you would enjoy helping with examples. We want to show how a suggested room can accidentally become a confirmed venue in a copied message.

The arrangements are still provisional, so please do not make travel plans from this letter. I will write when the teacher confirms the time and place. If you have a confusing fictional notice we could discuss, I would like to hear your idea. Best wishes, Bih.
